content.statement: Given two strings s and t, return true if t is an anagram of s, and false otherwise.
content.output_format: Boolean: true if t is an anagram of s, else false.

constraints.name: length
constraints.explanation: Bounds ensure linear solutions are needed; quadratic can be too slow.

constraints.name: alphabet
constraints.value: s and t consist of lowercase English letters
constraints.explanation: Enables 26-length fixed counter for optimal O(1) space.

notes: If Unicode or mixed-case is allowed, use a hash map instead of fixed 26 array.

test_cases.name: Anagram basic
test_cases.explanation: Both strings have identical character counts.

approaches.name: Sort and Compare
approaches.time_explanation: Sorting both strings dominates with O(n log n) where n = |s| = |t|.
approaches.space_explanation: Space for sorted copies or intermediate arrays/strings.
approaches.explanation: Sort both strings and compare equality. If they match, t is an anagram of s. This is simple and reliable but not optimal.

python.code:
def is_anagram(s: str, t: str) -> bool:
    return sorted(s) == sorted(t)

approaches.name: Frequency Map
approaches.time_explanation: Single pass to count characters and compare; n = |s|.
approaches.space_explanation: k = number of distinct characters (up to n or alphabet size).
approaches.explanation: Use a hash map (dictionary) to count characters in s and decrement for t. Finally verify all counts are zero. Works for arbitrary character sets.

approaches.name: Fixed 26 Counters
approaches.time_explanation: Single pass increment/decrement over characters; n = |s|.
approaches.space_explanation: Constant-sized array of length 26 for lowercase letters.
approaches.explanation: Early exit if lengths differ. Maintain an integer array of size 26; increment for s, decrement for t. Finally check all zeros.

trick.summary: Exploit fixed lowercase alphabet to use a 26-length counter for O(1) space.
details: Check lengths first to fail fast.
Map 'a'..'z' to indices 0..25 and adjust counts in one pass.
Final all-zero check proves equal multiset of characters.
